T. K. Long prosecuting attorney of
Morton county and Ed. Drury, deputy
sheriff came np Sunday. night to enfoi ee
the law passed during the last legis
lature, compelling the liquor" dealers of
unorganized comities to pay a county
license to the senior counties. Partial
payments were made by the liquor men
and the whole will probably bo paid.
We very much doubt the constitutional
ity of this law and by all. means advise
our liquor men to.make a test case and
fight It ant. It is worth the trial iU any
event nnd* this is undoubtly only an
entering wedge to.:|nrther taxation.

A meeting to organize ii bucker trig
ode was hold in the. rink last Monday
evening. It was called to order by J. C.
Fisher and A. T. Packard was elected
chairman. The necessity of such an
organization was.unanimously conceded!
On motion, a committee of five was
appointed, the names of J. C. Fisher, Jos.
A. Ferris, Marquis do Mores, F. D. Foster
and J. B. Walker, being-suggested and
adopted. This committee was authorized
to go ahead and perfect all
arrangements.
They met Tuesday evening and decided
to purchase buckets, ladders, hooks, axes
&cM the money to be raised by subscrip
tion. The force-pump and pipe at the
Marquis' house may also be bronght into
requisition.
